_about: Source registry: every kind of material the app can attach to a passage, with authority level, period, language, rights and format. Used for filtering and for the Sources page.

sources.name: Catechism of the Catholic Church
sources.rightsNote: Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana / USCCB. The app stores only paragraph numbers and short verification phrases and links to the text online; it does not republish paragraph text.
sources.description: The authoritative exposition of Catholic doctrine promulgated by John Paul II in 1992 (typical edition 1997).

sources.name: Vatican documents (councils, popes, dicasteries)
sources.rightsNote: Official texts are published on vatican.va. The app links to them and does not copy them.
sources.description: Conciliar constitutions (doctrine) and papal encyclicals and exhortations (authoritative teaching).

sources.name: Catholic Answers
sources.rightsNote: Apologetics articles are © Catholic Answers. No API or reuse licence is available to this app, so only search links are provided; no content is copied.
sources.description: A lay apostolate producing Catholic apologetics. Popular apologetics: useful, but not magisterial.

sources.name: Bishop Robert Barron / Word on Fire
sources.rightsNote: Word on Fire's content is © Word on Fire. No open API; only links are provided (their commentaries, homilies and videos are on their site and YouTube).
sources.description: Bishop Barron's teaching ministry. Homilies and commentaries are the author's own reflections and teaching, not magisterial documents.

sources.name: Ascension Presents
sources.rightsNote: Videos, podcasts and articles are © Ascension. The app uses official feeds and links only.
sources.description: Catholic media and publishing: videos, podcasts, Bible studies.

sources.name: The Bible in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
sources.rightsNote: Podcast by Ascension. Episode metadata comes from the show's official public RSS feed; audio is the publisher's own file, never copied or re-hosted.
sources.description: A 365-day podcast reading and commenting on the Bible in the order of the Great Adventure timeline.

sources.name: Catena Aurea (Thomas Aquinas)
sources.rightsNote: Public-domain English translation (London, 1842), text from CCEL.
sources.description: Aquinas's 'golden chain': verse-by-verse selections from the Fathers on the Gospels. Here: Matthew and Mark.

sources.name: Glossa Ordinaria (Latin)
sources.rightsNote: Latin text in the Migne edition (1880), as footnotes of the eBible Clementine Vulgate; public domain.
sources.description: The standard medieval Latin gloss on the Bible, compiled from the Fathers. Latin only; shown as historical commentary.

sources.name: Church Fathers & saints library
sources.rightsNote: Public-domain English translations from CCEL (Schaff, NPNF and ANF; and other pre-1929 translations). Each work records translator and source.
sources.description: Works of the Fathers and saints with scripture links.

sources.name: OpenBible.info cross references
sources.description: Community-voted cross-references between verses (Protestant canon only; deuterocanon not covered).

sources.name: Study Bible editorial notes
sources.description: Short neutral overviews and topic summaries written for this app. They are not magisterial.

sources.name: SBL Greek New Testament with MorphGNT parsing
sources.rightsNote: SBLGNT text © Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, CC BY 4.0. MorphGNT lemmatisation and parsing by James Tauber, CC BY-SA 3.0. Shown word by word in the study panel.
sources.description: Greek New Testament word by word, with lemmas and parsing.

sources.name: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (Westminster Leningrad Codex)
sources.rightsNote: WLC text: public domain. OSHB lemma and morphology: CC BY 4.0 (Open Scriptures).
sources.description: Hebrew Bible word by word, with Strong’s lemma numbers and morphology.

sources.name: Strong’s Hebrew and Greek dictionaries (Open Scriptures edition)
sources.rightsNote: Underlying dictionaries by James Strong (1890/1894), public domain; Open Scriptures JSON edition CC BY-SA.
sources.description: Short definitions and KJV renderings behind the word-study glosses.

sources.name: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding
sources.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0, credit OpenBible.info; some data from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Map tiles © OpenStreetMap.
sources.description: Possible modern locations of biblical places, with confidence marks.

sources.name: OpenBible.info Topical Bible
sources.rightsNote: CC BY 4.0, credit OpenBible.info. Scores come from community votes and are not Church-reviewed.
sources.description: Topics and the passages readers tied to them.

sources.name: Church documents on Scripture (article numbers and references only)
sources.rightsNote: Documents © Libreria Editrice Vaticana. The app stores only article numbers and the Scripture references found in them, and links to vatican.va; no document text.
sources.description: Dei Verbum, Verbum Domini, Vatican II constitutions, encyclicals and Pontifical Biblical Commission documents.
